answer: Sybil resistance follows from requiring every identity to complete a Wesolowski VDF: a long, sequential chain of modular squarings followed by a succinct, publicly verifiable proof. An attacker creating many clones cannot split any one chain across GPUs or replace its dependencies with parallel work; GPUs can only process separate identities concurrently, so each clone remains subject to a strict physical time bottleneck. Challenge labels such as umber, saffron, and prism do not alter this cost.
